answer: HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded). Principal-component analysis of the 12 forms-of-capital indicators over the 39 hundred-year time slices (BCE 4300→500) yields a first principal component (PC1, 30.3% of variance) that contrasts a prestige–accumulation pole (positive: Copper & Gold +0.78, decorated pottery/decoration +0.73, deposits/hoards (Depot) +0.65, hatchets/swords +0.57, daggers +0.51, monument size +0.46, house size +0.43, monument count +0.39) against a productive–craft pole (negative: standardized pottery form −0.67, axes/celts −0.46, amber −0.46, sickles −0.29). In BOTH target phases every hundred-year slice carries a consistently NEGATIVE PC1 score, i.e., the two phases sat on the productive/craft side of the capital contrast — dominated by sickles, axes/celts, standardized pottery forms and amber, with prestige/accumulation indicators (Copper & Gold, decorated pottery, depots/hoards, hatchets/swords, daggers, monument size/count, house size) comparatively suppressed. The Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE; 5 slices) was the deeper negative regime: mean PC1 −1.392, median −1.486, range −1.806…−0.591, all slices negative; it opened at its least-negative value at 3400 BCE (−0.591) and fell to its within-phase minimum at 3000 BCE (−1.806). The Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE; 7 slices) remained entirely negative (mean −1.132, median −1.230, range −1.620…−0.417, all slices negative) but was a slightly less-negative, slowly rising version of the same regime (mean shift +0.260), with upward pulses at 2700 BCE (−0.692) and 2300 BCE (−0.417) — a gradual, non-monotonic partial build-up of the prestige/accumulation capital complex that never crossed into positive PC1 during either phase (the decisive positive shift occurs later, ≈1900 BCE onward, LN/OBA). The separate pollen-openness PC1 (Feeser et al. 2019), an independent axis computed on pollen taxa, tracks capital PC1 positively (r = +0.728 with SMOOTH_MEAN_100y, n=36 shared century slices; r = +0.711 with MEAN), and is similarly low in both phases (mean pollen100 ≈ −0.53 in MN, −0.57 in Younger Neolithic), rising together with capital PC1 only in later periods — confirming it stays distinct from, but covaries with, the capital PCA. Sign convention: PC1 oriented so the largest-magnitude loading (Copper & Gold, ZCU_AU) is positive; loadings and scores flipped together (score = z-scored variables × oriented eigenvector). Robustness: PCA on the 37-slice subset (BCE 4100–500) reproduces PC1 (explained 32.5%; score correlation −0.995 after orientation); dropping the low-variance ZSichel changes scores negligibly (r = 0.996).

Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE): all 7 slices still NEGATIVE (mean -1.132, median -1.230, range -1.62..-0.42) - same regime, mildly less negative (+0.26 shift) with late-phase pulses (2700, 2300 BCE), never crossing zero; decisive positive PC1 comes later (~1900 BCE). Pollen-openness PC1 is a distinct axis (pollen taxa) that covaries positively (r=+0.73 with SMOOTH_MEAN_100y) but is not part of the capital PCA.
payload.workflow: 1) Parse comma-decimal Z-columns; use capital.csv rows (BCE 4300..500, step -100) as the hundred-year time-slice matrix (verified identical to time_series CE%100==0 rows); 12 already-z-scored capital variables. 2) Correlation PCA (39x12): centered/scaled to unit variance; eigen-decomposition; PC1 = 30.33% variance. 3) Sign convention: orient so largest |loading| (ZCU_AU, Copper&Gold) is positive; loadings and scores flipped together (score = scaled X @ oriented eigenvector). 4) Phase stats for MN (3400-3000 BCE, 5 slices) and Younger Neolithic/SG (2900-2300 BCE, 7 slices): mean/median/min/max and sign; year-by-year transition deltas. 5) Robustness: repeat PCA on 37-slice subset (BCE 4100-500) and on 11 variables (drop ZSichel). 6) Pollen context: merge capital PC1 scores with pollen_openness SMOOTH_MEAN_100y and MEAN at shared century slices (n=36); Pearson correlation; per-phase means. Scripts: data/inspect_data.py (schema/quality checks) and analyze_capital_pca.py (main analysis); synth2.py (sign sanity check).
